So `reorder_marks_arabic` is called with `i` and `end` being indices into `info` (the main buffer). Inside `reorder_marks_arabic`, it calls `buffer->merge_out_clusters (start, j)` where `start` and `j` are indices into `info`. But `merge_out_clusters` operates on `out_info`!

This is the bug. `merge_out_clusters` reads `out_info[start].cluster` and iterates `out_info[i].cluster` for `i` in `[start, end)`. If `out_len` is smaller than `end`, then `out_info[end-1]` etc. are uninitialized. This causes the use-of-uninitialized-value.

Let me look at the actual fix in harfbuzz history. The fix was to change `merge_out_clusters` to `merge_clusters` in `reorder_marks_arabic`. Let me verify by checking the current harfbuzz source.

Actually, let me look at the git blame / the actual fix. The bug is that `reorder_marks_arabic` should call `merge_clusters` (which operates on `info`) rather than `merge_out_clusters` (which operates on `out_info`).

Let me confirm by looking at the current upstream harfbuzz code. In current harfbuzz, `reorder_marks_arabic` calls `buffer->merge_clusters (start, j)`. Let me verify.

Actually, let me just build the fuzzer and reproduce. But first, let me understand what input triggers this. The fuzzer is `hb-fuzzer` which takes a font file as input. Let me look at the fuzzer.
